propositions: A configured provider='bedrock' is silently discarded when the model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical form like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), because _resolve_target treats any colon-bearing string as already provider-qualified
The _resolve_target function and infer_provider use two independent implementations of the same colon test, allowing them to diverge; they must call a shared split_provider_qualifier function
An explicitly configured provider must be checked and honored before scanning the model string for inline qualifiers, so that punctuation in model ids cannot overrule explicit configuration
An unresolved provider currently fails late at LLM call time with a misleading error message; it should fail fast at config-read time with clear naming of the class, provider, model, and reason
A bare model id with no configured provider still infers provider name as today, maintaining back-compatibility with unversioned aliases like 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6'
Conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pairs must raise LLMConfigError rather than silently selecting one, since either choice discards an explicit instruction
